bull_bear.body:
- customer lock-in: deep, long-duration customer relationships built on programme governance, service-level commitments and periodic technology refresh, supporting repeat business and cross-selling — evidence: the Company secured a Digital Workplace Solutions contract from Life Insurance Corporation of India valued at ₹138.44 crore and a Device-as-a-Service project from Jammu & Kashmir Bank valued at ₹74.99 crore during FY2025-26
- distribution: relationships with leading global technology providers give access to advanced platforms, training, technical support and collaborative go-to-market opportunities — evidence: strategic partnership announced with Cygeniq during the year to deliver AI-driven cybersecurity and trusted AI protection across India, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Rapid technology obsolescence and industry change — The technology industry is characterised by rapid change, intense competition, evolving customer expectations and continuing pressure to develop new capabilities, requiring ongoing investment in skills, certifications, platforms and partnerships.
- Execution risk on large, complex technology projects — Large technology projects may be affected by customer dependencies, site readiness, procurement schedules, product availability, logistics, OEM lead times and acceptance cycles.
- Working-capital intensity of large project engagements — Large projects may involve inventory funding, milestone-based billing and extended receivable cycles, requiring active treasury management, receivable reviews and inventory controls.
- Cybersecurity and data-protection exposure — The Company manages critical technology environments for customers and is expanding its use of cloud, automation and AI, which the AR flags as a significant and growing cybersecurity/data-protection risk.
- Competitive pricing pressure — Competition from global and domestic technology providers may result in pricing pressure and extended sales cycles.

business.body: Dynacons designs, supplies, implements and supports technology environments spanning data centre and cloud infrastructure, enterprise networking and cybersecurity, digital workplace and device lifecycle services, systems integration, Core Banking as a Service and managed services. It serves customers across BFSI, public sector and large enterprise segments, engaging across the full technology lifecycle from advisory and design through procurement, integration, deployment, monitoring, maintenance, refresh and secure retirement of technology assets.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Data Centre, Cloud and AI Infrastructure:** Enterprise servers, High-performance computing, Storage, Hyperconverged infrastructure, Virtualisation, Backup and disaster recovery, Private cloud, Hybrid cloud, Containerisation
- **Network, Connectivity and Cybersecurity:** Enterprise networking, SD-WAN, Wireless networking, Network monitoring, Next-generation firewalls, Endpoint security, Identity and access management, Security information and event management
- **Digital Workplace and Device Lifecycle Services:** End-user devices, Mobility, Virtual desktop infrastructure, Collaboration and audio-visual solutions, Managed print, Device-as-a-Service
- **Managed Services:** Infrastructure management, Data centre operations, Cloud operations, Network management, Security operations, Infrastructure monitoring, Service desk, Field support, Break-fix services, Staffing support

- distribution: relationships with leading global technology providers give access to advanced platforms, training, technical support and collaborative go-to-market opportunities — evidence: strategic partnership announced with Cygeniq during the year to deliver AI-driven cybersecurity and trusted AI protection across India, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Evolving from a traditional systems integrator into an integrated technology lifecycle partner, combining technology consulting, solution design, procurement, systems integration, project execution, managed operations, workplace support and asset lifecycle services under a unified delivery framework.
- Continuing to strengthen capabilities in AI-ready infrastructure, Data Centre and Cloud Solutions, Network and Cybersecurity, Digital Workplace Solutions, Device-as-a-Service and Managed Services, while maintaining a disciplined approach to project selection and execution.
- Deploying capital efficiently and investing selectively in opportunities that can generate sustainable long-term returns.
outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 Dynacons announced several significant engagements across its priority solution areas rather than a physical capex expansion: a Digital Workplace Solutions contract from Life Insurance Corporation of India (₹138.44 crore), additional orders of ₹51.28 crore for an advanced Core Banking as a Service solution and allied applications for State and District Cooperative Banks, an SD-WAN solution order from State Bank of India (₹62.98 crore), a Device-as-a-Service project from Jammu & Kashmir Bank (₹74.99 crore), and a private cloud infrastructure order from the Reserve Bank of India (₹750.82 crore). The Company positions this as broadening its footprint in mission-critical BFSI and public sector environments rather than adding manufacturing capacity, being an asset-light systems integrator and managed-services provider.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growth supported by sustained execution across Infrastructure Management Services, Data Centre and Cloud Solutions, Network and Security Solutions, Digital Workplace Solutions and large systems integration projects.
- Margin improvement supported by operating leverage, disciplined project execution and an improving mix of higher-value infrastructure and managed services engagements.
- Business model combines large project-based engagements with recurring and annuity-oriented services.
- Sizeable technology infrastructure and service engagements may involve advance procurement, inventory positioning, milestone-based billing, customer acceptance cycles and OEM lead times; the Company monitors receivables, inventory, project milestones and funding requirements accordingly.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
